Indicator constraints

Source: R/special-constraints.R
opt_indicator.Rd

opt_indicator(model, z, relation) imposes the linear relation only when the binary variable z equals active; otherwise the relation is free. SCIP handles indicator constraints natively. For other mixed-integer solvers they are reformulated exactly with big-M rows, where M is computed from the variable bounds; that requires finite bounds on the variables of the relation, and the solve stops with an error otherwise. No approximation is made.

Usage

opt_indicator(model, z, relation, active = 1, name = NULL)

Arguments

model

An opt_model().

z

A binary variable (scalar) or a vector of binaries, one per element of relation.

relation

A linear relation such as x + y <= 4.

active

1 (the relation holds when z = 1) or 0.

name

Optional name.

Value

An opt_special_constraint reference, invisibly.

Examples

# a fixed cost of 10 is paid when production x is positive
m <- opt_model()
x <- opt_variable(m, "x", lower = 0, upper = 8)
on <- opt_variable(m, "on", type = "binary")
opt_indicator(m, on, x <= 0, active = 0)
opt_constraint(m, x >= 3)
opt_objective(m, 2 * x + 10 * on)
opt_value(opt_solve(m), c(x, on))
#> [1] 3 1
